text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Centertel, the analogue mobile phone operator, has lowered prices of Nokia, Motorola and Benefon telephones in its third price cut from the beginning of this year, the company said.
- Chrysler and Mercedes car dealers around Poland will sell Excession bicycles assembled by the Kutno-based Fischer Centrum plant owned by Sobieslaw Zasada and Bernhard Fischer.

- Germany's EAU Hanseatische Aktiengesellschaft engineering firm and the PEC Siedlce heating and power plant have formed a joint venture to build an new heating and power plant worth 35 million marks.

- Up to 680,000 unemployed from Poland, Hungary, the Czech republic, Slovakia and Romania will emigrate to Germany every year after the countries join the European Union, the German DIW economic research institute said.

- Imoscar subsidiary of France's Carrefour supermarket chain will acquire the WZMot mechanical engineering firm worth $11 million. The company will build a trading centre at the WZMot site which will cost $30 million to build, the Wroclaw provicial governor's spokesperson Justyna Lewanska said.
- Average Pole consumes six kilograms of fish annually, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- The combined value of new share issues by Polish firms in 1997 will reach 5.4 billion zlotys, which shows a significant growth compared with 1.4 billion zlotys in 1996.
NOWA EUROPA
- 3Com netware producer and Computer Service Support firm have signed an agreement which will provide 3Com netware users with fast and professional maintenace service, the companies said.

- Imported parts for vehicles assembled by foreign automakers will have to enter the country in eight separate containers, Poland's economy ministry European integration department said. So far, Daewoo has transported assembly parts in six-container batches, which was harshly criticised by the European Commission.
- Polish Ocean Lines (PLO) shipping company earned its first net profits in 1996 after seven lean years, PLO's court appointed manager Miroslaw Hapko said.
- The listed Prochem engineering firm's net profit will reach four million zlotys in 1997, which shows a 20 percent growth compared with last year's results, a preliminary forecast said.
- The listed Exbud construction firm has increased its stake in the Elektromontaz Gdansk industrial assemblying firm to 76.8 percent, Exbud said.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- The Polish State Railways (PKP) are planning to buy railway engines and other rolling stock worth $8 billion by 2000, PKP said.
- Commercial Union (CU) has recently introduced a new Absolwent policy to allow parents finance the children's university education.
ZYCIE
- PZU insurance firm is considering a price reduction of the green card motor insurance policy, PZU spokesman Marek Maszek said.
- IBM Poland was awarded the Golden Mouse prize at the Komputer Expo'97 computer software and hardware fair.
PARKIET
- The listed Rafako boiler maker has installed a fluidal boiler at the Warsaw-based Zeran heating and power plant, Rafako said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
